name: agent-watch-status
description: Watch your coding agents from the status bar: one dot per session (working, waiting or idle), what each is doing, the files it changed, and a sound when it needs you. Supports Claude Code.
author: Carlos Santos

enumDescriptions: Only sessions started from this window: its Claude Code chats and its integrated terminals.
Sessions from this window plus any other session whose folder is inside this workspace.
Every Claude Code session running on this machine.
agentWatch.scope.description: Which sessions the chip shows. Sessions that belong elsewhere are listed but cannot be opened from this window.

agentWatch.showEmptySessions.description: Also show chats that have no messages yet. They are never opened from here: Claude Code cannot restore an empty chat and would start a new one instead.

agentWatch.showArchivedSessions.description: Also show idle sessions you archived in Claude Code. Archived sessions are always shown while they work or wait for you.

agentWatch.soundOnFinish.description: Play a short blip when a session in this window finishes its turn (goes from working to idle).

agentWatch.soundOnWaiting.description: Play a short alert when a session in this window stops to wait for your decision, such as a permission request (goes from working to waiting).

agentWatch.finishSoundFile.markdownDescription: Absolute path of a `.wav` file to play instead of the built-in finish blip. Try it with **Agent Watch: Play Finish Sound**.

agentWatch.waitingSoundFile.markdownDescription: Absolute path of a `.wav` file to play instead of the built-in waiting sound. Try it with **Agent Watch: Play Waiting Sound**.

agentWatch.minTurnSeconds.description: Turns shorter than this many seconds finish quietly: no finish blip, no system notification and no mention in the chip. 0 announces every turn.

agentWatch.notifyOnWaiting.description: Show a notification with an Open button when a session in this window stops to wait for your decision.

agentWatch.desktopNotifications.description: While this window is minimized or behind another window, also show a system notification when one of its sessions finishes its turn or stops to wait for your decision (notify-send on Linux, Notification Center on macOS).

enumDescriptions: Start order: every dot keeps its position when its status changes.
Waiting first, then working, then idle.
agentWatch.order.description: Order of the dots, the hover list and the session picker.

enumDescriptions: Keep sessions in the same branch or worktree together, in the chip, hover, picker and panel.
agentWatch.groupBy.description: How sessions are grouped. Sessions sharing a working tree end up together, which shows agents that may step on each other.

agentWatch.icon.markdownDescription: Icon at the start of the chip: `agent-watch-robot` (the extension's robot, as in the activity bar) or any codicon, such as `robot` or `sparkle`.

agentWatch.iconReflectsStatus.description: Color the icon with the most urgent status: red if any session is waiting, yellow if any is working.

agentWatch.maxDots.description: Maximum number of dots; the rest are grouped as +N.

agentWatch.hideWhenEmpty.description: Hide the chip when no sessions are running. The usage rings stay.

agentWatch.showUsage.description: Show how much of your Claude plan's 5-hour and weekly usage limits is used, as two rings after the chip with the percent inside, red from 80% on. Their hover lists every limit, and a click shows how long until each resets. Read from the last reading Claude Code took, dimmed once it is over 30 minutes old; hidden when there is none, such as when signed in with an API key.

agentWatch.dots.description: Character shown for each status. A status bar item has a single text color, so colored emoji are what make the dots differ.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No agent sessions are running in this window.

Start one in Claude Code, or show sessions from other windows with the [Scope setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22agentWatch.scope%22%5D).

colors.description: Color of the ring for the 5-hour usage limit, after the Agent Watch chip.
Color of the ring for the weekly usage limits, after the Agent Watch chip.
Color of a usage limit's ring, after the Agent Watch chip, once 80% of the limit is used.
